items.title: Marquee/primetime game flavor badge is buildable from data that already exists but has never been surfaced
items.executionEvidence: New pure module public/lib/marqueeBadge.js (deriveMarqueeBadge) derives Division Showdown/Playoff Preview/Statement Game labels deterministically from latestStandings, gated to week 6+. Wired into the schedule table (tabOverview.js renderSchedule) and the Sim-Watch overlay header (simWatchDirector.js renderHeader). test/marquee-badge.test.js: 12/12 pass, covering all three labels, the no-signal null case, the week-6 boundary, determinism, and malformed-input safety.
items.premise: public/lib/simWatchDirector.js:33 already computes and renders a rivalry-specific 'RIVALRY WEEK' banner with a heat label and win-streak text, proving the schedule/game-context data needed for editorial framing exists. Grepping every public/lib/*.js file for primetime|nationally televised|marquee|SNF|MNF|TNF returns zero hits — no equivalent day/time-based marquee framing exists for games that are not rivalry games (e.g. two division leaders meeting in week 10, or a defending-champion road game). This is presentation-only over existing standings/schedule state, not a variant of the rivalry banner, Sim-Watch, or any shipped gamification system.
evidence: public/lib/simWatchDirector.js:33 (existing rivalry-only banner pattern to model the new badge on)
items.constraint: Must derive marquee-ness deterministically from existing standings/record/rivalry state at schedule-render time; must not fabricate a broadcast network or invent viewership data; local-only, no backend.
verification: a game between the two current division leaders (or two teams with top-4 records) in week 6+ renders a 'Primetime' badge on the schedule and Sim-Watch entry point
badge label is deterministic from league state (record delta, division standing, rivalry heat) with no randomness
a game with no qualifying signal renders no badge (no false-positive marquee spam)
badge is covered by a direct Node test against constructed schedule fixtures

L1.recipe: Add a pure `isMarqueeGame(game, standings)` helper (top-4 records or division-leader clash) and render a static 'Primetime' badge on the schedule row when true; no new label variants.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a short deterministic label ('Division Showdown', 'Statement Game', 'Playoff Preview') selected from the qualifying signal, surfaced on both the schedule panel and the Sim-Watch overlay header, with a direct test asserting label selection against constructed standings fixtures.

L3.recipe: L2 plus weaving the badge into the existing news ticker as a pre-game flavor line and into the weekly rehearsal panel's context summary, reusing the same qualifying-signal helper so all three surfaces stay in lockstep.

items.title: No player-facing 'predict the spread' engagement loop exists anywhere in the shipped feature set
items.executionEvidence: New pure module public/lib/spreadPredictions.js (submitPrediction/resolveWeekPredictions/scorePrediction, localStorage-backed, keyed per-league) plus DOM surface public/lib/predictionPanel.js, mounted at #weeklyPredictionsPanel in game.html and wired from tabOverview.js renderSchedule() for every game in the current week (not just the controlled team's). test/spread-predictions.test.js: 18/18 pass, including a deep-frozen-object byte-identical-before/after proof that submission+resolution never mutate the game/schedule/league objects passed in. test/prediction-panel.test.js: 9/9 pass covering the empty state, pick form, pending/resolved-correct/resolved-incorrect receipts, and markup escaping.
items.premise: Grepping public/lib for spread|betting line|vegas|point spread|over/under|predict.*margin returns nothing resembling a pick'em mini-game. The simulation already computes team power/rating differentials (used internally for game simulation), which is exactly the input a local score-margin prediction UI would need. This is distinct from the Monday-Morning-QB counterfactual replay (post-game, alternate-history, non-canon) and from the plan rehearsal's 'predicts no result' disclaimer (which concerns the rehearsal never spoiling or biasing the simulation engine itself) — a player-authored pre-game guess that is scored against the real outcome afterward is a different, purely engagement-side mechanic with no engine feedback path.
evidence: grep -riE "predict|spread|moneyline" public/lib -> only non-matching hits in seasonEpilogue.js/seasonChapters.js/tacticalFilmRoom.js/architectPlanRehearsal.js (unrelated usages, one is a disclaimer string)

docs/DECISIONS.md 2026-07-02 'Counterfactual features must be explicitly non-canon and side-effect free' establishes the pattern this feature must also follow: deterministic, local, zero mutation of standings/stats/saves
items.constraint: Must be explicitly non-canon and side-effect-free per the existing counterfactual-feature decision pattern: the player's prediction never feeds into simulation odds, AI behavior, or any save-affecting state. Local-only persistence of the player's own prediction history and accuracy streak; no wagering of in-game currency or resources tied to franchise state.
verification: player can submit one predicted winner + approximate margin per upcoming game before it simulates
after the game resolves, the panel shows predicted vs actual with a correct/incorrect receipt and a running local accuracy streak
prediction never alters game simulation inputs, standings, or any persisted league state — direct test asserts league state is byte-identical with and without a submitted prediction
empty/no-prediction state renders cleanly with no forced interaction

L1.recipe: Local-only winner-only pick (no margin) for the current week's controlled-team game, scored after simulation, with a simple correct/incorrect toast; streak stored in localStorage.

L2.recipe: L1 plus point-margin guess, a running accuracy card (season streak, best streak, hit rate), and extending picks to all games in the current week (not just the controlled team), with a direct test proving zero engine-state mutation.

L3.recipe: L2 plus a season-long leaderboard-style summary in the season epilogue naming the player's best/worst predicted weeks, and a shareable 'prediction card' text export in the same style as the existing League Story Card.

items.title: A touchdown-flourish sound cue is fully defined but never played
items.executionEvidence: public/lib/simWatchDirector.js exports a pure shouldPlayTdFlourish(snapshot) gate (fires only on forward-advance 'tick'/'next' reasons whose current play is a touchdown, never on scrub-back/speed/pause) called from renderFrame() to invoke the existing playSound('td-flourish'), which already gates on the sound-enabled setting. test/td-flourish.test.js: 7/7 pass, covering TD-fires, non-scoring/field-goal no-fire, no-refire-on-scrub-back, and pregame-safety.
items.premise: public/lib/audioFeedback.js:95-99 defines a 'td-flourish' note sequence inside PALETTE, but grepping every playSound(...) call site across public/ (public/app.js:555,2243, achievements.js:255, rewardBeats.js:74,112,136, tabOverview.js:1069) shows only advance-tick, trophy-unlock, win-chime, loss-thud, draft-brass, sign-thunk, and tier-fanfare are ever invoked. td-flourish is a built, zero-marginal-cost immersion asset sitting dead in the palette.
evidence: grep -n 'playSound(' public -> 7 call sites, none pass 'td-flourish'
items.constraint: Must trigger only on an actual touchdown scoring event already surfaced by the simulation (not a heuristic guess), and must respect the existing sound-enabled settings toggle exactly like every other playSound call.
verification: playSound('td-flourish') fires exactly once per touchdown scoring play surfaced during Sim-Watch or box-score rendering
no call fires when the sound setting is disabled, matching existing playSound gating
no regression to existing win-chime/loss-thud/tier-fanfare call sites

L1.recipe: Wire playSound('td-flourish') into the existing Sim-Watch key-play advance path when the current play's type is a touchdown.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a direct test asserting the call fires on a touchdown play fixture and does not fire on a non-scoring play, using the existing sound-toggle test pattern from rewardBeats.test.js.

L3.recipe: L2 plus differentiating the flourish for the controlled team's touchdown vs an opponent's (reusing win-chime/loss-thud's existing team-relative pattern) so the cue is emotionally directional, not neutral.

items.premise: public/lib/dynastyTimeline.js:77 renders each season as a plain `<div data-idx=...>` with no role, tabindex, or aria-expanded, and line 97-106 binds expand/collapse only to a mouse 'click' listener. The component is live and wired via public/lib/tabSettings.js:14,708,914, but grepping test/ for dynastyTimeline or tl-node returns no matches — this shipped, wired UI surface has never been keyboard- or screen-reader-accessible.
evidence: public/lib/tabSettings.js:14,708,914 (live mount confirming this is a shipped, reachable surface)

verification: each season node has role="button", tabindex="0", and aria-expanded reflecting activeIdx state

focus order across nodes matches visual left-to-right order
a direct test drives the module in Node/jsdom and asserts the ARIA attributes and keydown behavior

L2.recipe: L1 plus aria-expanded reflecting activeIdx, aria-controls pointing at the detail panel (matching the S76 stats aria-controls pattern), and a direct test covering keyboard activation and ARIA state.

items.title: Cap War Room's expiring-contract counter cannot count a contract already at 0 years remaining
items.executionEvidence: Extracted the inline cap-projection loop in public/lib/engagementFeatures.js into a pure, exported computeCapProjection(roster, currentYear, opts) function and changed the expiring-count boundary from `yearsRemaining === 1` to `yearsRemaining <= 1`. New test/cap-war-room.test.js: 6/6 pass, covering 0-year counts, 1-year no-regression, 2-year exclusion, mixed rosters, and committed/dead-money splitting.
items.premise: public/lib/engagementFeatures.js:451 increments the current-year 'expiring' counter only when `yearsRemaining === 1`. Since the S67 offseason fix made `yearsRemaining: 0` a real, legally reachable mid-season state (the whole point of that fix was making contract expiry reachable at all), a contract sitting at exactly 0 years remaining before the offseason sweep runs would be invisible to this specific UI counter, even though it is arguably more urgent than a 1-year contract.
evidence: context/CURRENT_STATE.md 2026-08-01 entry confirms yearsRemaining:0 is now a real reachable state post-S67 fix
items.constraint: Display-only change to the expiring counter's boundary condition; must not touch the contract-write-side logic that the S67 decision already fixed.
verification: a roster fixture with a contract at yearsRemaining === 0 in the current year is counted as expiring
a roster fixture with yearsRemaining === 1 still counts as before (no regression)
a direct test constructs both fixtures and asserts the counter

L1.recipe: Change the boundary to `yearsRemaining <= 1` for the current-year expiring count.

L2.recipe: L1 plus a direct test with both a 0-year and 1-year contract fixture asserting both are counted and a 2-year contract is not.

L3.recipe: L2 plus visually distinguishing already-expired (0) from expiring-soon (1) in the rendered bar tooltip so the GM can tell the two states apart at a glance.
